title: President {{Warren}} addresses the press
situation: You are watching, not playing any of the three: it is 9:24 PM on November 10th, the night before, and the President of the United States, {{Warren}}, is speaking at a lectern in front of the press. President {{Warren}}: “At 6AM this morning, a national curfew was declared. Civilian movement will be strictly controlled, the right to assembly is suspended, all electronic communications are restricted, and I have granted enhanced powers to our security agencies. In addition to these measures, all androids must be handed over to the authorities immediately. Temporary camps are being set up in all our major cities to contain and destroy them. I am now asking all civilians to co-operate with the authorities, and rest assured that everything in our power is being done to guarantee the security of our nation.”

outcomes.0: The journalists all call out at once: “Please! Madam President!” You choose whose question she takes.

adaptationNote: Off-chart opening of the chapter (template 32.5 section “President Warren talks to journalists”, NOV 10TH, 2038, PM 09:24; the wiki infobox’s “9:24 AM” is the open question 23, the game string wins). The player watches as no protagonist, so the scene is a Player scene with no facts of its own; the module teaches the President’s statement (curfew, all androids to be handed over, camps to destroy them) to all three characters, who would have heard it. The template’s cut line (“My highest priority…”) is not built. No stat change.

title: The reporters’ questions
situation: You are watching President {{Warren}}’s press conference. The journalists shout over each other for her attention, and you decide which question she takes next. She will not stay for many.

options.text: HACKING: take the question on androids hacking critical systems.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that the androids could hack our IT systems, like nuclear power plants and military bases?” President {{Warren}}: “All androids working on sensitive sites have been neutralized and all IT systems have been suspended to avoid any risks of hacking. The situation is under control.”

options.text: DEVIANT LEADER: take the question on the deviants’ leader.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Has the leader of the deviants been apprehended?” President {{Warren}}: “The deviant that is known as {{Markus}} has not been located yet, but we will soon track it down and neutralize it.”

options.text: WORRYING THEFT: take the question on the missing cobalt and the robbed weapon stores.
options.outcome: Journalist: “A convoy of medical cobalt is reported missing. Army weapon stores are also said to have been robbed. Can you confirm these reports?” President {{Warren}}: “I have no information on that at this time.”

options.text: {{CYBERLIFE}}: take the question on what happens to the android maker.
options.outcome: Journalist: “What’s gonna happen to {{CyberLife}}? Will androids be banned definitively?” President {{Warren}}: “We’re working very closely with {{CyberLife}} to neutralize all deviants. I won’t make any comments about anything else until we have dealt with the android question.”

options.text: INTELLIGENT LIFE: take the question on androids as a new form of life.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Many believe that androids are a new form of intelligent life. Do you have any comment?” President {{Warren}}: “That’s ridiculous. Next question, please?”

options.text: DEVIANTS: take the question on how many deviants are still loose.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that a large number of deviants are still on the loose?” President {{Warren}}: “We don’t have the full reports at this time, but if so, I can assure you they will soon be apprehended and destroyed.”

options.text: RECALL CENTERS: take the question on the camps and history.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Some say these camps awaken painful memories from human history. How do you respond to that?” President {{Warren}}: “That’s absurd. There’s absolutely no connection. Androids are not living beings. All we are doing is destroying defective machines.”

options.text: {{JERICHO}} ASSAULT: take the question on last night’s raid.
options.outcome: Journalist: “What can you tell us about the assault that happened last night?” President {{Warren}}: “The FBI raided an abandoned freighter in {{Detroit}} at 10:45 PM yesterday. Several thousand androids were destroyed or captured. Our forces are now combing the streets to ensure that none got through the net. We are going to find them one by one and destroy them.”

options.text: ARMY: take the question on androids in the armed forces.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Is it true that androids make up 60% of the armed forces? Is our army still able to ensure our homeland security?” President {{Warren}}: “We neutralized all military androids the second their reliability came into doubt, we have called the National Guard for reinforcement. Our armed forces are fully operational and are able to ensure our homeland security.”

options.text: PUBLIC OPINION: take the question on how the public sees the deviants.
options.outcome: Journalist: “Madam President, public opinion seems to be particularly hostile to the deviants because of their violent behavior. Can you give us your perspective on that?” President {{Warren}}: “The deviants have proved to be very violent so far. They have demonstrated that they are a menace to society and I have every intention of eliminating them.”

adaptationNote: The template’s one prompt of ten reporters’ questions, in the template’s order with its labels, as a repeatable scene: each question asked drops out. The wiki says the player can have “up to 4 or 5” answered before the game moves on; the benchmark takes four, then President {{Warren}}: “Thank you. That will be all.” (unsourced choice between the wiki’s two figures). {{JERICHO}} ASSAULT is offered only if {{Jericho}} was raided (template unlock “Jericho was attacked”). DEVIANT LEADER names {{Markus}} while he is alive, otherwise “The deviant leader has not been located yet” (template variant “Markus is dead and North is leading the revolution”). PUBLIC OPINION has the template’s two variants, “positive” and “negative”; the benchmark reads “positive” as public opinion at least Sympathetic, the same line the demonstration’s last stand uses (open question 1 asks whether Indifferent already counts). Each answer is taught to {{Markus}}, the one it concerns. No stat change.
